name: Rave
description: Light on the feet, bouncy and repetitive. Built to last for hours on a crowded floor. Danced to Techno, House, Trance and Hard dance, usually around 124–150 BPM. Each move card has the cues and a beat to count along to: try it, then mark whether you could do it.

source.name: Written for Study Buddy as a casual primer.

questions.prompt: Rave bounce: how does it go?
answers: A light, springy bounce through the balls of the feet, with the chest and shoulders loose.
steps: Weight on the balls of your feet, heels just off the floor
Bounce through the ankles on each beat, knees soft
Let the chest pop forward a little with each bounce
Shoulders loose, hands relaxed at waist height
questions.explanation: Rave floors run for hours. A low-effort bounce is what lets you dance from the first track to the last. Tip: Keep it small, and it'll last all night. Tip: Swap to the knee bounce now and then to rest your calves.
questions.note: Watch out for: jumping off the floor on every beat, which tires you out in one track.

questions.prompt: Running man: how does it go?
answers: Run on the spot: one knee lifts while the standing foot slides back, then they swap.
steps: Stand on your left foot and lift the right knee
On the beat, put the right foot down in front while the left foot slides back
Lift the left knee on the 'and', bringing the foot through
Put it down in front while the right foot slides back, and repeat

beat.counts: Lift on 'and', slide on the beat

questions.explanation: Tip: Practise in socks on a smooth floor so the slide is easy. Tip: Learn it slowly at 100 BPM, then raise the tempo.
questions.note: Watch out for: hopping instead of sliding; leaning back: keep the chest a little forward.

answers: The standing foot swivels heel-toe to travel sideways while the other leg kicks out.
steps: Stand on your left foot with the right knee lifted
Swivel the left foot: toes out, then heel out, moving you to the left
At the same time, kick the right foot out to the side on each swivel
After four swivels, switch legs and travel the other way
questions.explanation: Tip: Learn the swivel alone first, holding on to a chair. Tip: Smooth floors and trainers help; grippy boots make it hard.
questions.note: Watch out for: travelling too far on a busy floor. Two swivels and back is plenty.

questions.prompt: Arm wave: how does it go?
answers: A ripple that travels from one hand, through the shoulders, to the other hand.
steps: Arms out to the sides at shoulder height
Lift the left wrist, then elbow, then shoulder, one after the other
Pass it across: right shoulder, right elbow, right wrist
Each joint drops as the next one rises
questions.explanation: Tip: Practise one joint at a time in front of a mirror. Tip: Bring it out on the breakdown, when everyone slows down.
questions.note: Watch out for: moving the whole arm at once, so it never ripples.
